Intersect a band with linear restrictions on coefficients

Source: R/shape-confidence-set.R
shape_confidence_set.Rd

Represent the set of coefficient vectors whose evaluated functions are inside an initial band and satisfy supplied linear inequalities and equalities.

Usage

shape_confidence_set(
  X,
  lower,
  upper,
  Ain = NULL,
  bin = NULL,
  C = NULL,
  d = NULL,
  level = 0.95,
  interpretation = c("confidence", "credible"),
  band_type = c("unspecified", "simultaneous", "pointwise")
)

in_shape_set(object, coefficients, tolerance = 1e-08)

Arguments

X

A finite numeric matrix that maps coefficients to function values at the evaluation points. Each column corresponds to a coefficient.

lower, upper

Numeric vectors of lower and upper limits, one per row of X. Infinite limits are allowed. Missing values are not allowed.

Ain

A finite numeric matrix defining inequalities Ain %*% b >= bin. It must have the same number of columns as X. NULL means no inequalities.

bin

A finite numeric vector, one entry per row of Ain. If NULL, zero is used for every inequality.

C

A finite numeric matrix defining equalities C %*% b = d. It must have the same number of columns as X. NULL means no equalities.

d

A finite numeric vector, one entry per row of C. If NULL, zero is used for every equality.

level

A number strictly between zero and one recording the nominal level of the initial band. This does not calibrate the band.

interpretation

Is the initial band a confidence or credible band?

band_type

Record whether the initial limits were calibrated jointly ("simultaneous"), separately at each evaluation point ("pointwise"), or whether their calibration is unspecified ("unspecified", the default).

object

A set created by shape_confidence_set().

coefficients

A finite numeric vector, or a finite numeric matrix with one candidate coefficient vector in each column. Rows must correspond to columns of object$X in the same order; names are not used for matching.

tolerance

A finite non-negative number used as an absolute tolerance in function values and constraint residuals. The default is 1e-8. Setting it to zero uses exact floating-point comparisons. Multiplying a constraint row by a constant changes the effect of an absolute tolerance.

Value

shape_confidence_set() returns a list of class "shape_confidence_set" containing X, lower, upper, Ain, bin, C, d, level, interpretation, and band_type. Missing constraint matrices are stored as matrices with zero rows. in_shape_set() returns a logical vector, one value per candidate coefficient vector.

Details

The returned object represents the set $$\{b: \mathrm{lower} \le Xb \le \mathrm{upper},\quad A_{in}b \ge b_{in},\quad Cb=d\}.$$ The matrices are retained explicitly; the function does not optimise over the set, test whether it is empty, or draw samples from it. Redundant and inconsistent restrictions are allowed. Inconsistent restrictions represent an empty set.

The initial band restricts function values only at the supplied evaluation points. The extent of the shape restriction depends on the supplied coefficient inequalities. For example, appropriate spline coefficient inequalities can guarantee monotonicity throughout a spline's domain, whereas differences between evaluated function values guarantee it only on that grid. This function does not infer restrictions from a fitted model or extend restrictions between evaluation points.

If the true coefficient vector satisfies the supplied restrictions, it is in the intersection exactly when its evaluated function is in the initial band. Thus intersection preserves the coverage of an initially valid simultaneous confidence band, for truths satisfying those restrictions. Pointwise limits alone do not supply a simultaneous confidence set. For credible bands, the same posterior probability statement requires the posterior to be supported entirely on the restricted coefficient space. Intersection does not fix smoothing bias, invalid initial calibration, or an incorrect restriction.

Coordinatewise minima and maxima of functions in this set need not themselves belong to the set. This matters for coupled restrictions such as an integral equal to one: two ordered functions with that integral must coincide almost everywhere. Retaining the whole set avoids assigning such equalities to separate endpoint curves.

Examples

# Two non-negative masses whose sum is one.
region <- shape_confidence_set(
  X = diag(2), lower = c(0.1, 0.2), upper = c(0.8, 0.9),
  Ain = diag(2), C = matrix(c(1, 1), nrow = 1), d = 1,
  band_type = "simultaneous"
)
in_shape_set(region, c(0.4, 0.6))
#> [1] TRUE
in_shape_set(region, c(0.4, 0.7))
#> [1] FALSE
